sourceLocations.location: IBCC RHC capture p. 10, 'zeroing the catheter & verification'
sourceLocations.note: Zero at the mid-axillary line; as a check, the sternal manubrium about 5 cm above the right atrium reads about +4 mmHg (proportionate to the module's figure). Treats leveling and zeroing as one step; no 7.4 mmHg figure.

sourceLocations.note: Not cited by these surfaces. Separate zeroing and leveling sections; phlebostatic axis about 5 cm below the sternal angle supine; above underestimates, below overestimates, in proportion to column height. No number.

items.topic: Fast-flush response and what damping does to systolic, diastolic and mean

learnerSurfaces.locator: Pressure system section, validity check 'Dynamic response', What you check
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: prompt return with one or two rapidly decaying oscillations, a sluggish rounded return, or persistent ringing.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Waveform interpretation, display problem 'Overdamped measurement system', Why no chamber can be named (also practice tracing 6)
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: so systolic reads low and diastolic reads high while the mean stays relatively preserved.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Same display problem, Repair or re-read first
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: then classify the fast-flush release before interpreting anything but the mean.

items.learnerWording: “Perform a fast flush from a confirmed, safe position and watch the release: prompt return with one or two rapidly decaying oscillations, a sluggish rounded return, or persistent ringing.” Overdamped: “systolic reads low and diastolic reads high while the mean stays relatively preserved.” Repair: “…classify the fast-flush release before interpreting anything but the mean.”
items.visual: Model-drawn overdamped PA display (rounded upstroke, blunted peak, narrowed pulse pressure, notch largely lost).
items.intendedTeachingPoint: The flush release tells you whether the system can reproduce rapid pressure change; an overdamped system under-reads systolic and over-reads diastolic, so shape-dependent readings wait for repair.

sourceLocations.location: Bootsma Part 1, §2.5.1 Damping, p. 11 (PDF 7)
sourceLocations.note: Not cited by these surfaces. Repeated fast-flush test; optimal damping shows 1.5–2 oscillations, more means underdamped, fewer overdamped; underdamped over-reads systolic and/or under-reads diastolic, overdamped the reverse. Nothing on the mean.

sourceLocations.location: Ragosta ch. 2, pp. 15–16 (Fig. 2.1) and pp. 33–34 'Common Errors and Artifacts'
sourceLocations.note: Overdamping loses the notch and reads systolic low and diastolic high; underdamping the opposite. No fast-flush test; nothing on the mean or pulse pressure.

sourceLocations.location: IBCC RHC capture pp. 16–17
sourceLocations.note: Same directions; no fast-flush test or oscillation count.

sourceCheck.result: Directions of error are supported. 'One or two' oscillations approximates Part 1's 1.5–2. No checked document states that the mean is relatively preserved.
sourceCheck.notChecked: Saugel 2020 (the registered source for fast-flush patterns) was not available.

items.clinicalQuestion: Is 'one or two rapidly decaying oscillations' an acceptable teaching rendering? Is 'the mean stays relatively preserved' supported, and by which source? The recognition practice's repair advice ('before interpreting anything but the mean') depends on it.
items.hold: The mean-preserved statement and the repair advice that relies on it are held at authored-claim depth.

items.topic: A mixed-compartment (false) wedge value is not a PAWP and must not feed PVR

learnerSurfaces.locator: Troubleshooting atlas, 'False wedge from incomplete occlusion', numbers teaching
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: It is not a valid PAWP and must not be entered into PVR or other derived calculations.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Same entry, why it matters
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: A falsely elevated PAWP can misclassify pre-capillary physiology as post-capillary disease and redirect treatment toward an unsupported mechanism.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Same entry, actions
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: compare a wedged-tip sample with a simultaneous systemic arterial saturation; low systemic saturation limits discrimination.

items.learnerWording: “The displayed value is a mixture of PA and wedge compartments. It is not a valid PAWP and must not be entered into PVR or other derived calculations.” “A falsely elevated PAWP can misclassify pre-capillary physiology as post-capillary disease…” “…compare a wedged-tip sample with a simultaneous systemic arterial saturation…”
items.visual: Atlas figure of residual PA pulsatility on an atrial-type contour; the live capstone labels its PAWP invalid.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: An invalid input is rejected before any derived number is calculated from it; the confirmation is physiological, not cosmetic.

sourceLocations.location: Ragosta ch. 2, p. 35 (hybrid tracing); p. 25 and Fig. 2.37 p. 40 (oximetry)
sourceLocations.note: Incomplete occlusion mixes PA and wedge waveforms and reads falsely high; in pulmonary hypertension it can suggest decompensated heart failure or mitral stenosis. Wedge-position saturation above 90% is the strongest confirmation. A hybrid trace may still show a and v waves. Nothing on PVR.

sourceLocations.location: IBCC RHC capture pp. 25–26
sourceLocations.note: Not cited by this entry. Under-wedging reads falsely high and makes PVR falsely low; a wedge sample should be within 5% of systemic saturation. Over-wedging: steadily rising trace, wedge above PA diastolic, or wedge at under 1–1.5 mL.

sourceLocations.location: Bootsma Part 1, §2.5.3 Overwedging and underwedging, pp. 11–12
sourceLocations.note: Criteria for overwedging (above PA diastolic, rising until deflation, non-pulsatile, wedging under 1.5 mL).

sourceLocations.location: Whitener 2014, p. 332
sourceLocations.note: Only notes that a sample drawn while wedged is arterialized.

sourceCheck.result: The rejection rule and the misclassification risk are supported. Sources state the oximetry confirmation differently (above 90%; within 5% of systemic); the module gives no number.
sourceCheck.notChecked: Whether the derived evaluator's withholding covers every mixed-compartment case in the cases.

items.clinicalQuestion: Confirm the teaching. Should the oximetry confirmation carry a number, and which? Should the 'residual PA pulsatility' cue add that a hybrid trace can still show a and v waves?

items.topic: Balloon inflation, prompt deflation, and what to do when the PA waveform does not return

learnerSurfaces.locator: PAWP capture section, sequence step 4 'Commit'
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: Inflate only from a confirmed pulmonary-artery position, to the volume specified by the manufacturer for the catheter in use, and never with liquid.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Sequence step 7 'Deflate'
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: Deflate promptly and deliberately, as a step of its own. Occlusion is brief; nothing about the value obtained is a reason to keep it inflated.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Sequence step 9 'Continue?'
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: treat the signal and the catheter position as unsafe: stop, do not flush or manipulate the catheter, and escalate.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Troubleshooting atlas, 'Spontaneous wedge', actions
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: When permitted, withdraw slowly until a clear PA waveform returns.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Troubleshooting atlas, 'Overwedging', warning
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: Stop inflation immediately. Allow passive balloon deflation. Do not flush.

items.learnerWording: Commit: “Inflate only from a confirmed pulmonary-artery position, to the volume specified by the manufacturer for the catheter in use, and never with liquid.” Deflate: “Deflate promptly and deliberately… Occlusion is brief…” Continue?: if the PA waveform did not return, “stop, do not flush or manipulate the catheter, and escalate.” Atlas: spontaneous wedge “When permitted, withdraw slowly until a clear PA waveform returns.”; overwedging “Stop inflation immediately. Allow passive balloon deflation. Do not flush.”
items.visual: Live simulator: balloon inflation blocks every exit, the reducer refuses a flush while wedged or balloon-up, and a 10-second automatic release (a simulator rail, not the learner's deflation).
items.intendedTeachingPoint: Occlusion is a brief, deliberate act that ends by the learner's own deflation and is confirmed by a returning PA waveform.

sourceLocations.location: Bootsma Part 1, p. 6 (insertion); §2.3.4 Wedge position, p. 8; §2.5.3, pp. 11–12
sourceLocations.note: Balloon takes 1.5 mL of air. Once wedged, deflate and do not advance; the PA waveform should reappear, and if not, retract about 2 cm. Inflating when migrated distally may rupture a small vessel. No time limit; nothing on liquid or flushing.
1.5 mL of air; a catheter left wedged or in a small branch can cause infarction or PA rupture.

sourceLocations.location: IBCC RHC capture p. 10; pp. 23–24; p. 13
sourceLocations.note: 1.5 mL of air; PA rupture is the main major complication, avoid unneeded wedges; wedging at under 1 mL means too distal.

sourceLocations.location: IntelliVue MX750/850 IFU, 'Measuring Pulmonary Artery Wedge Pressure' pp. 256–257, 'Editing the Wedge' p. 257, warnings p. 258
sourceLocations.note: Monitor prompts inflation and deflation and stores the trace. Warning: prolonged inflation can cause pulmonary hemorrhage or infarction, so inflate minimally; if PAWP mean exceeds PA systolic, deflate and report. P. 256 equates wedge pressure with LV end-diastolic pressure, a device-manual simplification the module does not adopt.

sourceLocations.location: Not available
sourceLocations.note: Registered for balloon-inflation and placement safeguards; not checked.

sourceCheck.result: Brief occlusion, deflation and confirming PA return are supported. 'Never with liquid' and the no-flush rules were not found in any checked document (the catheter IFU was unavailable). Step 9's 'do not … manipulate the catheter' differs from Part 1's 'retract about 2 cm' and from the atlas's 'withdraw slowly when permitted'.

items.clinicalQuestion: When the PA waveform does not return after deflation, should a learner be taught to stop and escalate without manipulating the catheter, or to withdraw about 2 cm / slowly when permitted? Make step 9 and the atlas agree. Confirm 'never with liquid' and the no-flush rules against the current catheter IFU.
items.hold: Both instructions stay as authored; the difference is recorded, not resolved. Simulator interlocks are unchanged.

learnerSurfaces.locator: PAWP capture, outcome 'Atrial morphology with late a and v waves', next action
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: Read at end expiration — the end-diastolic point if you are estimating left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, the mean if that is the value you want, and not the two interchangeably.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Sequence step 3 'Predict'
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: the mean typically sits a little below pulmonary-artery diastolic pressure

learnerSurfaces.locator: Sequence step 6 'Plausible?'
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: In sinus rhythm that includes the a wave; in atrial fibrillation it does not

items.learnerWording: “Read at end expiration — the end-diastolic point if you are estimating left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, the mean if that is the value you want, and not the two interchangeably.” “…the mean typically sits a little below pulmonary-artery diastolic pressure…” “In sinus rhythm that includes the a wave; in atrial fibrillation it does not…”
items.visual: Model-drawn wedge tracing with a and v waves after the QRS and T.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: Name which wedge value you are reading and read it at end expiration; a plausible wedge sits just below PA diastolic.

sourceLocations.location: Ragosta ch. 2, p. 21 (end expiration); pp. 24–26 (wedge waveform, West zones, PEEP)
sourceLocations.note: End expiration; mean PCWP about 0–5 mmHg below PA diastolic unless PVR is raised; no a wave in atrial fibrillation; only zone 3 reflects LA pressure. Reports only the mean; with large v waves the nadir of the x descent best predicts LVEDP.

sourceLocations.location: Whitener 2014, pp. 329–330
sourceLocations.note: End-expiratory values in spontaneous and mechanical ventilation; monitors display the mean; the a-wave peak best estimates LVEDP; a wave lost in atrial fibrillation.

Not cited by these surfaces. PAWP at the end of the a wave or before the QRS at end expiration, ideally the mean of three readings; West zone 3 required. Compares PAWP with mean PA pressure; a wedge above PA diastolic suggests a non-zone-3 position or overwedging.

sourceLocations.location: IBCC RHC capture pp. 23–27
sourceLocations.note: Not cited by these surfaces. End expiration (peak on spontaneous breathing, trough on the ventilator); end diastole about the mean of the a wave; in atrial fibrillation use the c wave; PA diastolic about 1–4 mmHg above the wedge.

sourceCheck.result: End expiration, the relation to PA diastolic and the atrial-fibrillation statement are supported. Where the end-diastolic point sits is placed differently in each source (end of the a wave or before the QRS; a-wave peak; about the a-wave mean; x-descent nadir with large v waves). The module does not name it.

items.clinicalQuestion: Should the module name where the end-diastolic point is read, and if so which convention? Should atrial-fibrillation guidance (one source: use the c wave) be added?
